requirements.statement: ERP's synchronous database access has exactly one engine-construction site, app/db/__init__.py's get_engine(), which builds a plain SQLAlchemy Engine via create_engine(...) — the exact shape a Kernel-successor DatabaseRuntime constructor's `engine` parameter accepts. No second sync create_engine(...) call site exists anywhere else under app/, so ERP's synchronous session requirement is expressible against the Kernel successor without any new Kernel API.

Every ERP symbol that constructs or depends on an async database engine/session (AsyncSession, get_async_engine, get_async_session_local, AsyncSessionLocal, create_async_engine, get_async_db, get_async_db_for_org) lives only in nine files — app/db/__init__.py, app/rls.py, app/services/finance/common/numbering.py, app/services/finance/settings_web.py, app/services/people/settings_web.py, app/web/deps.py, app/web/finance/settings.py, app/web/people/settings.py, app/web/settings.py — and none of those nine files imports dotmac_kernel. ERP's async database paths are therefore self-contained and product-owned, independent of which sync DatabaseRuntime ERP composes. Async support is explicitly TRANSITIONAL: this record declares that status as ERP's stated position, not as a completion or permanence claim, and does not assert that async is or will be required of the Kernel API.

ERP owns explicit post-fork hook points independent of any Kernel disposal API — @worker_process_init.connect in app/celery_app.py (Celery prefork) and post_worker_init(worker) in gunicorn.conf.py (Gunicorn preload_app worker spawn). Fork safety for a composed Kernel-successor engine is satisfiable by calling runtime.engine.dispose() from these existing hooks; no fork-safety API needs to exist on the Kernel successor.

MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL (the BYPASSRLS-capable credential) appears under app/ only as a named constant/docstring reference in app/runtime_admission.py and app/migration_credential_custody.py — never bound to a live engine or session in application runtime code — and no app/ call site passes a bypass_rls=True (or similarly named) flag to a session or engine constructor. ERP therefore has no runtime cross-tenant BYPASSRLS mechanism today; any future genuinely fleet-wide need is expressible as a separately bound engine (the Kernel successor's platform_engine constructor parameter shape), never a per-call session flag.

ERP applies statement_timeout and pool sizing via connect_args/pool kwargs at create_engine() call time inside app/db/__init__.py's _get_connect_args()/get_engine(), before any Kernel DatabaseRuntime would ever receive the resulting Engine object. This is satisfiable through the DatabaseRuntime constructor's existing engine: Engine parameter, with no new Kernel surface required.

ERP's tree names exactly one legacy (pre-module-lineage) tenant GUC needing compatibility alongside the canonical app.current_tenant setting: app.current_organization_id, primed in app/rls.py's set_current_organization/set_current_organization_sync alongside app.current_tenant in the same transaction-local statement. This is a single, stable, named value — the shape a legacy_tenant_settings-style compatibility parameter would need to accept, not an open-ended or growing set.

No app/ source file sets or reads a bypass_rls-named PostgreSQL GUC (app.bypass_rls or similar) at runtime; app/rls.py's own module docstring states plainly that 'runtime code cannot assert a PostgreSQL RLS bypass.' The GUC-based cross-tenant bypass mechanism this record's companion document (docs/architecture/erp-runtime-async-pid-fork-contract.md) describes as being retired has already been fully removed from app/ as of this record's revision — there is no live writer left to retire.

As of this revision, no file under app/ imports dotmac_kernel.session_runtime, DatabaseRuntime, bind_database_runtime, or resolve_database_runtime. This record states requirement EXPRESSIBILITY only — that ERP's synchronous session needs can be met by the Kernel successor's existing public surface — and makes no adoption or composition claim. A pin in pyproject.toml is installation, not adoption.

composition.declaration: dotmac-kernel is pinned at the exact version 0.1.0a98 from the forgejo private index (no range operator).
Ten consume-pure dotmac_kernel modules are composed under app/: assembly, capabilities, features, licensing, money, planes, prerequisites, profiles, providers, testing.
One adopted persisted kernel symbol, dotmac_kernel.cache.TenantScope, is composed in app/tenancy.py.
One adopted persisted kernel symbol, dotmac_kernel.models.Tenant, is composed in app/services/tenant_projection.py.
dotmac_kernel.session_runtime.DatabaseRuntime is NOT composed anywhere under app/ — the sync-runtime successor is pinned but not adopted.
